title: POC incremental precision sprint chronicle
content:
Summary:

This doc is a working chronicle of a 3-week solutions-eng sprint for a mid-market customer POC where the primary goals were: keep 95th percentile inference latency under 350ms for 512-token requests, reduce per-token cost by 40% relative to baseline FP16 model, and maintain ROUGE/QA accuracy degradation < 3 points on core prompts. The engagement focused on an incremental precision (staged quantization + intelligent fallback) approach rather than a single aggressive quantization step.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: Fintech SME, real-time chat summarization and classification, strict PII handling (needs private deploy option).
- Hardware: Target Dedicated pool (A100-like) for baseline; plan for lower-tier T4-like nodes for cost tier.
- Models considered: open-weights LLaMA-2-13B, Mistral-7B-instruct, Falcon-40B-instruct (served as high-accuracy fallback).
- Feature surface to demo: latency-aware routing, prefix KV caching, precision cascade (FP16 -> INT8-GPTQ -> 4-bit dynamic), prompt trimming and response-length gating.

Decisions from workshop day 1:
- Use Mistral-7B-instruct as primary candidate for median-case (good cost/latency). LLaMA-2-13B chosen for mid-accuracy tier; Falcon-40B reserved as fallback for high-confidence regeneration when precision cascade fails QA checks.
- Quantization path: start with 8-bit GPTQ (per-channel where possible) for Mistral and LLaMA. If 8-bit meets latency but fails quality, try mixed-precision: key/value matmul in INT8, attention softmax in FP16. For latency-first runs, trial Q4/DQ (4-bit) with block-wise outlier handling.
- KV caching: enable prefix caching for conversation context > 128 tokens. Cache warm-up policy: cache initial system + user history up to 256 tokens, evict LRU.

Sprint experiment matrix (high level):
- A: FP16 baseline (Mistral-7B) on A100: throughput, latency, quality.
- B: GPTQ INT8 (Mistral-7B) on A100: measure latency reduction and QA drop.
- C: GPTQ INT8 (Mistral-7B) on T4: verify cost gains and latency SLO headroom.
- D: Mixed-precision (INT8 compute + FP16 softmax) on A100: quality vs B.
- E: Q4 dynamic (Mistral) with outlier tokens in FP16: aggressive cost test.
- F: Cascade: route first to INT8; if QA confidence < threshold or hallucination score > threshold, fallback to LLaMA-2-13B INT8; if still bad, escalate to Falcon-40B FP16.

Early results (week 1 runs):
- A (FP16) median latency: 210ms; p95: 420ms; tokens/sec baseline: 120
- B (GPTQ INT8) median latency: 160ms; p95: 310ms; tokens/sec: 160; QA drop: 1.6 points (within target)
- C (INT8 on T4) median latency: 300ms; p95: 620ms (T4 noisy), tokens/sec: 70; QA drop similar to B. Not acceptable for strict latency SLO on T4 for p95.
- D (mixed-precision) p95 improved to 280ms with QA drop 0.9 points; promising hybrid approach.
- E (Q4 dynamic) median latency 120ms but QA drop 4.8 points — unacceptable without additional mitigation.

Operational notes and playbook decisions:
- Staged rollout: start production demo with INT8-GPTQ + mixed-precision safe guards. Only enable Q4 for background/batch summarization where latency SLOs are relaxed.
- Confidence math: define a composite score (logit-stability + likelihood ratio + external classifier) for live QA gating. Set soft threshold at 0.65; below that trigger rerun on LLaMA-2-13B INT8. If second attempt score < 0.7, escalate to Falcon-40B FP16 and mark event in trace.
- Cost accounting: track per-route token cost in Console; show customer expected monthly cost under 3 traffic profiles (50k, 200k, 1M requests).
- Prompt pipeline changes: 1) length-prefilter to remove redundant system tokens; 2) compress user history using extractive summarizer when history > 512 tokens; 3) reduce max output tokens with deterministic truncation rules in low-cost mode.

Workshop artifacts and action items:
- Action: engineering to add mixed-precision kernel toggle to canary image (owner: Evan). ETA: 2025-11-13.
- Action: add KV cache metrics to per-route dashboard (owner: Priya). ETA: 2025-11-10.
- Action: create regression test suite for QA metrics with canonical prompt set (owner: Maya). ETA: 2025-11-08.
- Action: draft customer-facing runbook for fallback behavior and SLA expectations (owner: Liam). ETA: 2025-11-12.

Unresolved questions / risk log:
- GPTQ toolchain variance: different GPTQ exporters produce different weight layouts; we need to standardize exporter + checksum validation for model artifacts. Risk: silent quality drift across deploys.
- Rare token outliers cause large attention activations; need a strategy for token-level dynamic precision (hot-token FP16 paths) — prototype idea in notes but untested.
- T4-class hardware p95 variance suggests Dedicated pool composition matters; recommend demo on A100-like hardware, propose separate cost-workload plan for edge T4.

Notes to self / heuristics captured during session:
- If QA delta < 2 pts and p95 improved by >20% with INT8, prefer INT8 for routes with >5000 req/day.
- Use prefix-only caching for multi-turn chat; avoid caching responses that include sensitive PII unless customer agrees to encrypted cache key storage.
- For prompt trimming, always keep the latest user turn and last system prompt; compress older turns.

Appendix: quick checklist for POC handoff
- Artifact list: model wheel (GPTQ-int8-mistral-7b-2025-11-01.tar), mixed-precision-canary:v0.3, canonical-prompt-set.csv, latency-trace-samples.jsonl.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350ms on demo hardware; QA drop <= 3 pts vs FP16 baseline; fallback correctness verification tests pass (synth prompts).
- Demo script: 1) show cached vs uncached latency; 2) show INT8 route with degraded prompt and automated fallback; 3) show cost dashboard scenarios.

End of chronicle.

Raw workshop notes (short bullets):
- "user complained about hallucination on birthdates" -> add numeric entity mask in prompt to reduce hallucination.
- "try MACRO batch 8 for throughput runs" -> batch schedule conflicts with latency SLO, keep at 1 for p95-sensitive routes.
- "consider spline-based tokenizer trimming to preserve semantics when compressing history" -> research spike.
- link to bench PR for mixed-precision kernels: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/214
